title: architect-spotlight-three-slide-vignette-draft
content:
Purpose: a compact 3-slide vignette sellers and SEs can drop into a 10–12 minute technical intro for integration architects. Draft: terse, skimmable, and geared to leave the architect with a clear pilot checklist and minimal followups.

Slide 1 — 60s: What the architect needs to know (30–60s opener)
- Opening line: "We make inference predictable: same API surface from dev to private infra with ops controls to meet latency and cost SLOs."
- Top benefits for architects (bullets to say out loud):
  * Predictable tail-latency with SLOs and automatic fallbacks
  * Control plane that preserves network/topology requirements for VPC/on-prem deployments
  * Observable unit economics: token-level latency + cost, route-level breakdowns
- Quick credibility: two numbers to drop (example):
  * Typical 99th-percentile reduction when enabling smart batching + KV caching: ~35–50% (customer pilot median)
  * Reduced per-token spend via quantization suggestions: 20–35% in evaluation studies
- Quick call-to-action: "If you have a single endpoint we can sniff for 15 minutes, we can baseline latency/cost and propose a 4-week pilot."

Speaker notes (1): keep to 90 seconds. If they ask for architecture, pivot to slide 2. If they immediately ask about data residency, follow bullet on private deployments.

Slide 2 — 5 minutes: How it fits in your stack (technical quickview)
- Visual (verbal description for the 3-slide): client -> Redwood API (hosted/dedicated/private) -> serving runtime (GPU pool) -> observability/rollouts. Point out where network, routing policies, and KMS sit.
- Key integration checkpoints to call out:
  * Authentication & traffic flow: token-based API key or mTLS (private) — ask which they prefer
  * Egress constraints: can we place a tiny bastion in their VPC to access models vs on-prem package?
  * Latency budget: typical 95/99 SLOs we can achieve on Dedicated; ask for their P50/P95 goals
  * Data controls: customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and optional local-only inference runtime
- Fallback & resilience design (talking bullets):
  * Multi-variant routing: primary model (high quality, heavier HW) -> cheaper quantized fallback -> region fallback
  * Canary rollouts + auto-rollback on quality regressions tied to evals/prompt sets
- Quick demo script (30–60s to show in console):
  1) Show per-route latency histogram (filter: last 1h)
  2) Toggle a canary: route 10% to a quantized instance and show live cost delta
  3) Open the rollout and show auto-fallback policy config

Developer/SE cheat bullets for deep followup:
- Required information for a scoped pilot: expected qps, typical prompt lengths (tokens), auth mechanism, VPC egress constraints, compliance needs (SOC2/iso), sample prompt set for quality baseline
- Quick checklist to hand to infra team: open ports, NACL rules, KMS approver, pull request template for IaC to roll the agent/bastion

Slide 3 — 3 minutes: Pilot checklist + decision map (clear next steps)
- 4-week pilot template (minimal friction):
  Week 0: kickoff + network check + sample prompt collection
  Week 1: baseline run (hosted) + perf/cost dashboarding
  Week 2: dedicated/private staging + canary routing
  Week 3: quality regression checks + ops runbook handoff
  Outcomes: latency report, per-token cost estimate, runbook + SLA proposal
- Decision map (simple):
  * Pass/fail criteria for moving to Dedicated/Private: meets P95 latency target AND per-token cost within X% of target (custom) AND no unresolved compliance blockers
  * If fail on latency: propose HW tier change or enable prefix caching; offer a short 2-week optimization sprint
  * If fail on quality with quantized models: show sample fallbacks and A/B evaluation plan
- Objection rapid responses (scripted micro-replies):
  Q: "We can just run open-source ourselves." A: "Yes—you can. The ROI case: time-to-production, continuous ops (rollouts/fallbacks), and observability that reduces incident MTTR. We also help pick quantization profiles that minimize quality regression."
  Q: "What about cost predictability?" A: "We provide reserved capacity for predictable throughput and token-level cost visibility; for pilots we ship a cost-sensitivity dashboard so you can see unit-economics change with batching/cache policies."

Appendix (notes to self / SE quick tips)
- Small phrases to include: "unit-economics", "canary + auto-rollback", "KV/prefix caching", "route-level SLOs"
- Metrics to capture during pilot: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, average batch size, cache hit rate, per-route cost per 1k tokens
- Typical friction points and recommended pre-emptive asks:
  * Network egress approvals (takes the longest) — get compliance/infra on calendar early
  * Sample prompts that exercise worst-case lengths (not just happy path)
  * Agreement on quality metric (e.g., top-1 exact match, BLEU, semantic-similarity threshold)

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing deck):
- What default numbers do we put for "cost within X%"? Should be configurable per segment — ask pricing.
- Do we include a live console screenshot or anonymized metric snapshot? (privacy approval)
- Can we get a canonical 3–4 prompt set from applied-ml to use as a pilot baseline?

Todo (action items for this file):
- @Marco: add a one-slide anonymized metric screenshot (temp snapshot)
- @Sofia: add compliance blurb for EMEA customers (data residency phrasing)
- Authors: iterate language to be <220 words so it fits a slide with speaker notes

Slack seeds and refs (for SE to copy):
- Quick DM template to infra lead: "We want a 15-min network check to approve a small bastion for Redwood pilot. Can you confirm outbound port policy and time window?"
- Template for prompt collection: short form asking for 10–20 representative prompts, worst-case length, and expected QPS

Sign-off checklist before external:
- Remove internal numbers or mark as internal-only
- Confirm linked compliance docs and KMS phrasing
- Run 1 internal dry-run with Solutions Eng to time the pitch (target 10–12 minutes)

Version notes: initial sketch — purposely terse. This is meant to be pasted as three slides in a lightweight deck or embedded in a salesperson's Slack DM as "three-slide architect vignette". Will iterate after Marco's screenshot and Sofia's compliance copy.

[notes-to-self] Keep phrasing engineer-first; avoid marketing-speak. Leave room for the architect to ask about last-mile network constraints — that's our hook for a technical kickoff.
